question: Of the following pairs of surface molecules, what is used by the virgin T lymphocytes to extravasate to the lymph node?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Virgin T lymphocytes" -> "express L-selectin" -> "bind to high endothelial venules (HEVs)" -> "express CCR7" -> "respond to chemokines CCL19/CCL21" -> "extravasate to lymph node" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Virgin T lymphocytes" -> "express L-selectin" -> "bind to high endothelial venules (HEVs)" -> "express CCR7" -> "migrate towards chemokine gradient" -> "enter lymph node" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Virgin T lymphocytes" -> "express L-selectin" -> "adhere to endothelial cells" -> "express CCR7" -> "chemotaxis towards lymph node" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Virgin T lymphocytes" -> "express L-selectin" -> "initial tethering and rolling on HEVs" -> "express CCR7" -> "firm adhesion and transmigration" -> "enter lymph node" -> 92%
analysis: Virgin T lymphocytes, also known as naive T cells, extravasate to the lymph nodes using specific surface molecules. CCR7 is a chemokine receptor that guides T cells to lymphoid tissues, and L-selectin (CD62L) is an adhesion molecule that facilitates the initial rolling of T cells on the high endothelial venules (HEVs) of lymph nodes. This combination is crucial for the homing of naive T cells to lymph nodes.
